AkkLove LAOS4-07 (X001001) – translation (Wasserman 2016)

Web: https://oracc.museum.upenn.edu/akklove/X001001/html

Project translation extracted from the ORACC HTML view (rank 3 in our hierarchy; consult only after our own reading).
Each paragraph: [first label – last label of the transliteration lines it translates] text. "## " = section heading.

[o 1]Come in, shepherd, Ištar’s lover, [o 2]Spend the night here, shepherd, Ištar’s lover, [o 3]At your entering, my father is happy for you, [o 4]my mother, Ningal, is rejoiced over you. [o 5]She served you oil in a bowl. [o 6]At your entering, the bolts rejoice over you, [o 7]the door itself shall be opened [for you]! [o 8]You, wooden bolt – what do you know? [o 9]What do you know? The entrance of my darling! [o 10]Indeed, I love, I love, oh, lusty one. [o 11]He freed his dogs ... [o 12](saying:) "Let me come in front of Ningal!" [o 13]After her bride entered in front of Ningal, [o 14]they divided the sweet cake in the bowl. [o 15]The illustrious one is worried about the dogs and shepherds. [o 16]- Why are they insulting (him)? He brought and offered. [o 17]He went and came back, he brought and offered, [o 18]Yes, the illustrious one is worried about the shepherds’ affluence. [o 19]The company is well, the king is well, [o 20]Dumuzi is well, Ištar’s lover. [o 21][... loosen,] loosen your sandals! [o 22][...] unpack your nets! [o 23][...] we shall eat, oh, lusty one! [o 24][...] oh, lusty one! [o 25][...] he refuses, he won’t bring. [o 26][...] we shall eat, oh, lusty one! [o 27][...] we shall sprinkle! [o 28][...]oh, lusty one! [o 29][...] the cry of your flock,[r 30][...] your lambs, [r 31][...] the cry of your flock, [r 32][...] neglect(?) our sheepfold! [r 33]Recite for me [his name/number], he wouldn’t let (it) go! [r 34][...] [r 35]Recite for me his name/number, he wouldn’t let (it) go! [r 36]Ištar went into his sheepfold, [r 37]opened her mouth and said to him: [r 38]"How sweet is the water, the water of your sheepfold! [r 39]your water murmurs, It is the water of (your) animal stall!" [r 40]'I shall sing on the heroic shepherd.' [r 41]Total 39 lines. [r 42]Series: 'O darling loving me.' [r 43]Library tablet of Taqšītum, son of Meme-Enlil, administrator of the temple of Ištar.
